# checkly_environment_variable (Resource)

Global environment variables that can be referenced from check scripts.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Simple Enviroment Variable example
resource "checkly_environment_variable" "variable_1" {
  key    = "API_KEY"
  value  = "loZd9hOGHDUrGvmW"
  locked = true
}

resource "checkly_environment_variable" "variable_2" {
  key   = "API_URL"
  value = "http://localhost:3000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The name of the environment variable. Changing the name forces the environment variable to be replaced.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The value of the environment variable, which must not be empty. At most 64000 bytes in UTF-8, or 31744 bytes for a secret or locked variable. A secret value has at least 3 characters. The API never returns the value of a secret variable, so the provider keeps the configured value: a change made outside Terraform, for example in the web app, doesn't show in the plan. An imported secret variable has a null value, so the first plan after the import shows an update, and applying it overwrites the value in Checkly with the configured one.

### Optional

- `locked` (Boolean) If true, the value is hidden in the Checkly UI by default, but it can be revealed. (Default `false`).
- `secret` (Boolean) If true, the value can never be revealed after creation, and the API never returns it; see `value`. The API can't turn a secret variable back into a regular one, so changing `secret` from `true` to `false` forces the environment variable to be replaced. (Default `false`).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the environment variable. Identical to the key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing environment variable using its key.
terraform import checkly_environment_variable.example API_KEY
```
